peoples.s: The largest ethnic group on Earth. Han Chinese make up about 90 percent of China's population and share a written tradition that stretches back more than three thousand years.
peoples.fun: Chinese characters are one of the oldest writing systems still in daily use, with roots in oracle-bone inscriptions about 3,300 years old.
peoples.special: The name Han comes from the Han dynasty (206 BCE to 220 CE), when a shared written culture spread across the empire.

records.text: Largest ethnic group in the world

peoples.s: A people of the Ganges delta known for a rich literary tradition. Bengali is the national language of Bangladesh, and the Language Movement of 1952 is commemorated each year as International Mother Language Day.
peoples.fun: International Mother Language Day, 21 February, honours Bengali speakers who protested for their language in Dhaka in 1952.
peoples.special: Rabindranath Tagore, a Bengali poet, won the 1913 Nobel Prize in Literature and wrote the words of the national anthems of both India and Bangladesh.

records.text: Tagore was the first non-European winner of the Nobel Prize in Literature

peoples.s: Named for the land of five rivers. Punjabis are among the largest peoples in South Asia and have large communities in Britain, Canada and the Gulf.
peoples.fun: Bhangra, a Punjabi harvest dance, has become a dance style performed around the world.
peoples.special: Langar, the free communal meal served in Sikh gurdwaras, is open to everyone regardless of background.

peoples.home: Tamil Nadu in India, northern Sri Lanka, Singapore
peoples.s: Tamil literature is more than two thousand years old, and Tamil is one of the oldest living classical languages.
peoples.fun: Tamil has a distinctive retroflex sound, written ழ, that few other languages share.
peoples.special: The Brihadisvara Temple in Thanjavur, completed in 1010 under the Chola dynasty, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

records.text: Tamil is among the oldest living classical languages

peoples.home: Southern and eastern Afghanistan, northwest Pakistan
peoples.s: The largest people in Afghanistan and a very large one in Pakistan. Traditional society is organised around tribes and a code of conduct called Pashtunwali.
peoples.fun: Melmastia, the Pashtun custom of hospitality, obliges a host to feed and protect any guest.
peoples.special: Khushal Khan Khattak, a 17th-century warrior and poet, is celebrated as a national poet of the Pashtuns.

peoples.s: One of the most homogeneous large nations. Japan combines an ancient imperial and Shinto tradition with a highly industrialised modern society.
peoples.fun: Written Japanese mixes three scripts at once: kanji, hiragana and katakana.
peoples.special: Wabi-sabi, an aesthetic that finds beauty in imperfection and impermanence, shapes tea ceremony, ceramics and gardens.

records.text: Nishiyama Onsen Keiunkan, open since 705, is recognised as the world's oldest hotel

peoples.home: Korean Peninsula, plus communities in China, the US, Japan, Russia
peoples.lang: Korean (a language isolate or Koreanic family)
peoples.s: Koreans share one language and history across two states. The Korean alphabet, Hangul, was created in the 15th century under King Sejong.
peoples.fun: Hangul was designed in the 1440s so that ordinary people could learn to read quickly. South Korea celebrates Hangul Day on 9 October.
peoples.special: Kimjang, the making and sharing of kimchi, is on UNESCO's list of intangible cultural heritage.

peoples.s: The largest ethnic group in Indonesia. Javanese court culture is known for gamelan orchestras, shadow puppetry and batik cloth.
peoples.fun: Javanese has speech levels, so the words you choose change with the age and status of the person you are speaking to.
peoples.special: Borobudur, a 9th-century Buddhist temple in Central Java, is often described as the largest Buddhist temple in the world.

records.text: Borobudur is often called the largest Buddhist temple in the world

peoples.s: The majority people of Vietnam. Vietnam also recognises 53 other ethnic groups, many living in the highlands.
peoples.fun: Vietnamese is written in Latin letters with accent marks that show its six tones, a system developed with European missionaries in the 1600s.
peoples.special: Tet, the Lunar New Year, is the biggest holiday of the year, when families gather and honour their ancestors.

peoples.s: A traditionally nomadic herding people who built the largest contiguous land empire in history under Genghis Khan in the 13th century.
peoples.fun: The Mongol Empire ran a relay messenger system called the Yam, with stations where riders could swap tired horses for fresh ones.
peoples.special: Naadam, a festival of wrestling, archery and horse racing, is on UNESCO's list of intangible cultural heritage.

records.text: The Mongol Empire became the largest contiguous land empire in history

peoples.home: Xinjiang, western China, and Central Asia
peoples.s: A Turkic, mostly Muslim people of the oasis towns along the old Silk Road. Their homeland is in the Xinjiang region of China.
peoples.fun: Uyghur Muqam, a classical musical tradition from Xinjiang, is on UNESCO's list of intangible cultural heritage.
peoples.special: Oasis cities such as Kashgar and Turpan were important stops on the Silk Road.

peoples.home: Arabian Peninsula, the Levant, North Africa
peoples.s: A people defined mainly by shared language and culture across 22 countries. Classical Arabic is the language of the Quran and a major medium of science and poetry in the medieval world.
peoples.fun: The word algebra comes from the Arabic al-jabr, the title of a 9th-century book by the mathematician al-Khwarizmi.
peoples.special: Scholars at the House of Wisdom in Baghdad translated and built on Greek, Persian and Indian science during the medieval period.

peoples.s: Heirs to the Achaemenid Empire of the 6th century BCE. Persian poetry by writers such as Hafez, Rumi and Ferdowsi is read across the world.
peoples.fun: The Persian Achaemenid Empire built the Royal Road and an early postal relay across its territory.
peoples.special: Nowruz, the Persian New Year, is celebrated at the spring equinox and has been marked for more than 3,000 years.

peoples.home: Turkey, Cyprus, Germany and the Balkans
peoples.s: Turkic peoples migrated from Central Asia into Anatolia from the 11th century. The Ottoman Empire, which lasted until 1922, shaped the modern state.
peoples.fun: Turkish coffee, brewed in a small pot called a cezve, is on UNESCO's list of intangible cultural heritage.
peoples.special: The Mevlevi sema, the whirling ceremony associated with the poet Rumi, is also on UNESCO's list.

peoples.home: Israel, the United States, France, Canada, the UK and elsewhere
peoples.lang: Hebrew, plus Yiddish, Ladino and local languages
peoples.s: An ancient people and religious community whose history begins in the Land of Israel. After centuries of dispersion, communities now live on every inhabited continent, and Hebrew is again a spoken national language in Israel.
peoples.fun: Hebrew was revived as an everyday spoken language in modern times, thanks largely to Eliezer Ben-Yehuda and others who worked on it from the 1880s.
peoples.special: Shabbat, a weekly day of rest, has been kept by Jewish communities for thousands of years.
known: Jewish communities developed languages of their own, including Yiddish in Central and Eastern Europe and Ladino among Jews of Spanish origin.
Homeland: Israel, the United States, France, Canada, the UK and elsewhere.

records.text: Hebrew is often described as the only language successfully revived from mainly religious use to a national spoken language

peoples.home: Southeastern Turkey, northern Iraq, Iran, Syria
peoples.s: One of the largest peoples in the world without a state of their own. Their homeland, Kurdistan, spans four countries.
peoples.fun: Newroz, the spring new year, is marked with bonfires and dancing in Kurdish communities.
peoples.special: Kurdish has two major groups of dialects, Kurmanji and Sorani, written in different scripts.

records.text: Among the largest peoples in the world without a state of their own

peoples.home: Armenia, plus Russia, the US, France, Lebanon
peoples.s: Armenia was the first state to adopt Christianity as its official religion, in 301 CE. The Armenian alphabet dates to the year 405.
peoples.fun: The oldest known leather shoe, about 5,500 years old, was found in the Areni-1 cave in Armenia.
peoples.special: The Armenian alphabet was created by Mesrop Mashtots in 405 CE and is still used today.

records.text: Armenia was the first state to adopt Christianity as its official religion, in 301 CE

peoples.s: Known for the ancient city-states of Ife and Oyo and for bronze and terracotta sculpture. Yoruba religious traditions also shaped practices across the Americas, such as Santería.
peoples.fun: Yoruba is a tonal language, and the talking drum (dundun) imitates the rise and fall of speech.
peoples.special: Ife, a Yoruba city, is known for naturalistic bronze and terracotta heads made centuries ago.

peoples.s: Traditionally organised in village democracies rather than kingdoms. Igbo-Ukwu bronzes date to about the 9th century.
peoples.fun: Bronzes found at Igbo-Ukwu, dated to about the 9th century, show highly advanced lost-wax casting.
peoples.special: The New Yam Festival, Iri ji, marks the harvest with feasting and dancing.

peoples.s: Hausa is a trade language across West Africa. The Hausa city-states, such as Kano, were centres of commerce and Islamic scholarship.
peoples.fun: Hausa was written for centuries in an Arabic-based script called Ajami before the Latin alphabet became common.
peoples.special: Kano, a Hausa city, has been a trading centre for roughly a thousand years, and parts of its old city wall still stand.

peoples.s: The largest ethnic group in Ethiopia. The traditional Gadaa system organised society into generational grades with elected leaders.
peoples.fun: UNESCO recognised the Gadaa system, in which leaders are chosen by generational grades, as intangible cultural heritage in 2016.
peoples.special: Irreecha, a thanksgiving festival held at the end of the rainy season, draws huge crowds each year.

peoples.s: The largest ethnic group in South Africa. In the early 19th century King Shaka forged the Zulu kingdom into a major regional power.
peoples.fun: Zulu beadwork uses colour combinations that can carry messages between people.
peoples.special: Zulu is the most widely spoken home language in South Africa.

peoples.s: Semi-nomadic cattle herders famous for red shukas, beadwork and the adumu jumping dance.
peoples.fun: A traditional Maasai greeting, Kasserian ingera, means 'And how are the children?'
peoples.special: Maasai have traditionally measured wealth in cattle, and their red shukas are among the most recognisable dress in East Africa.

peoples.home: Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya, the Sahara
peoples.s: The indigenous people of North Africa, present long before the Arab conquests. The Tuareg of the Sahara are one Amazigh group.
peoples.fun: Tifinagh, an ancient script, is still used to write Tamazight languages, and Yennayer, the Amazigh New Year, falls in mid-January.
peoples.special: Morocco (2011) and Algeria (2016) both recognise Tamazight as an official language.

peoples.s: The largest Slavic people and the biggest ethnic group in Europe. Russian is spoken as a first or second language across much of the former Soviet Union.
peoples.fun: Russian is written in the Cyrillic alphabet, which grew out of work by followers of the missionaries Cyril and Methodius in the 9th century.
peoples.special: The first matryoshka nesting doll was carved in the 1890s.

peoples.s: Germany was a patchwork of states until unification in 1871. Germans have shaped modern philosophy, music and science.
peoples.fun: In German, all nouns are written with a capital letter.
peoples.special: The Brothers Grimm collected folk tales in the early 1800s, preserving stories such as Hansel and Gretel.

peoples.pl: about 5 million in Ireland, many more abroad
peoples.home: Ireland, with large diasporas in the US, UK, Australia
peoples.s: Tens of millions of people worldwide claim Irish ancestry. The Great Famine of the 1840s drove one of the largest emigrations in European history.
peoples.fun: Irish (Gaeilge) is the first official language of the Republic of Ireland and has one of the oldest written traditions in Europe.
peoples.special: St Patrick's Day is celebrated by Irish communities and many others around the world every 17 March.

peoples.home: Basque Country, northern Spain and southwest France
peoples.s: Their language is unrelated to any other living language, and is thought to predate the arrival of Indo-European languages in Europe.
peoples.fun: Euskara, the Basque language, has no known living relatives.
peoples.special: Basque pelota, a handball-like game, is played on special courts called frontons.

records.text: Basque is Europe's best-known language isolate

peoples.home: Northern Norway, Sweden, Finland and Russia's Kola Peninsula
peoples.s: The indigenous people of northern Scandinavia. Many Sámi have herded reindeer for centuries.
peoples.fun: Sámi languages have a rich vocabulary for snow, ice and reindeer, reflecting generations of herding.
peoples.special: Joik, a traditional Sámi form of song, expresses a person, animal or place rather than telling a story about it.

peoples.home: Across Europe, especially the Balkans and Central Europe
peoples.s: Language and genetic studies trace the Roma to northern India about a thousand years ago. They are Europe's largest ethnic minority.
peoples.fun: The Romani flag and anthem were adopted at the first World Romani Congress, held near London in 1971. 8 April is International Romani Day.
peoples.special: Romani musicians influenced flamenco in Spain and the brass and string ensembles of Central and Eastern Europe.

peoples.home: The Andes of Peru, Bolivia and Ecuador
peoples.s: Descendants of the Inca and neighbouring peoples. Quechua is spoken today by millions and is an official language in Peru and Bolivia.
peoples.fun: The Inca built the Qhapaq Ñan, a road network of about 30,000 km across the Andes.
peoples.special: The Inca kept records with the quipu, a system of knotted cords.

peoples.s: Builders of Tikal and Chichén Itzá, with a hieroglyphic writing system and an advanced calendar. Maya communities and languages remain very much alive.
peoples.fun: Maya mathematicians used a symbol for zero in their number system.
peoples.special: The Maya used cacao in ceremonial drinks, long before chocolate reached Europe.

peoples.home: Navajo Nation, in Arizona, New Mexico and Utah
peoples.s: The Navajo Nation is the largest reservation in the United States. Navajo code talkers served in the US Marines in World War II.
peoples.fun: During World War II, Navajo code talkers developed a spoken code that was never broken.
peoples.special: Navajo weaving and silversmithing are admired and collected around the world.

records.text: The Navajo Nation is the largest reservation in the United States

peoples.s: Peoples of the Arctic who built a way of life around hunting and the sea ice. Nunavut, in Canada, was created as an Inuit-majority territory in 1999.
peoples.fun: Inuit developed the kayak, a boat built to move quietly while hunting on cold water.
peoples.special: The inuksuk, a stone landmark, helps people find their way and marks good hunting and fishing places.

peoples.s: Polynesian navigators who reached New Zealand around the 13th century. Te reo Māori is an official language of New Zealand.
peoples.fun: The haka, a ceremonial dance with chanting, is used for welcomes, farewells and challenges.
peoples.special: Whakapapa, or genealogy, connects people to their ancestors, to each other and to the land.

records.text: New Zealand was the first self-governing country to give women the vote in national elections, in 1893

peoples.pl: about one million, including Torres Strait Islanders
peoples.s: Among the oldest continuous cultures on Earth, with a presence on the continent for at least 50,000 years.
peoples.fun: The Budj Bim eel traps in Victoria, part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site, are thousands of years old.
peoples.special: Dreaming stories pass on knowledge of law, land and living things through story, song and art.

records.text: Among the oldest continuous living cultures on Earth

peoples.home: Ukraine, Poland, Canada, United States, and diaspora
peoples.s: The largest Slavic people after the Russians and Poles. Ukrainians have a distinct language, literature and folk tradition, and Ukraine became independent in 1991.
peoples.fun: Pysanky, Ukrainian Easter eggs, are decorated with wax and dye in a method much like batik.
peoples.special: Embroidered shirts called vyshyvanky carry regional patterns, and people in Ukraine still wear them on special days.

peoples.pl: about 60 million in Italy, with many more abroad
peoples.home: Italy, Argentina, Brazil, United States, and diaspora
peoples.s: Italy was a collection of kingdoms and city-states until unification in 1861. Italians gave the world the Renaissance, opera and much of Western art.
peoples.fun: Italy has more UNESCO World Heritage Sites than any other country.
peoples.special: Modern standard Italian grew out of the Tuscan dialect used by the poet Dante in the early 1300s.

peoples.home: France, Canada, Belgium, Switzerland, and diaspora
peoples.s: The French built one of Europe's oldest nation states. The 1789 Revolution, with its slogan of liberty, equality and fraternity, shaped modern ideas of citizenship.
peoples.fun: The traditional baguette was added to UNESCO's list of intangible cultural heritage in 2022.
peoples.special: French was the main language of European diplomacy for centuries, and it is still an official language of the United Nations.

peoples.home: Spain, with large communities in Latin America
peoples.lang: Spanish (Romance), plus Catalan, Galician and Basque
peoples.s: Spain's people grew out of Iberian, Roman, Visigothic and Moorish history. Spanish is now spoken by hundreds of millions of people around the world.
peoples.fun: Spaniards often eat dinner after 9 pm, later than in most of Europe.
peoples.special: Don Quixote, published in 1605 by Miguel de Cervantes, is often called the first modern novel.

peoples.pl: about 40 million in Poland, with millions more abroad
peoples.home: Poland, Germany, United Kingdom, United States, and diaspora
peoples.s: Poland was one of Europe's largest kingdoms in the 1500s. It vanished from the map for 123 years before returning as an independent state in 1918.
peoples.fun: Polish uses special letters such as ł, ą and ę that no other major European language uses in the same way.
peoples.special: Poland's Constitution of 3 May 1791 is among the earliest written national constitutions in the world.

peoples.s: Ancient Greece gave the world democracy, philosophy, theatre and the Olympic Games. Today's Greeks speak a language with more than 2,500 years of written history.
peoples.fun: The word alphabet comes from the first two Greek letters, alpha and beta.
peoples.special: The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens in 1896.

peoples.home: Philippines, United States, Gulf states, and diaspora
peoples.lang: Filipino (Tagalog) and English, plus many regional languages
peoples.s: The Philippines is made up of more than 7,000 islands, and Filipinos speak over a hundred languages. Millions work abroad and send money home.
peoples.fun: Filipinos are known for the longest Christmas season in the world, with carols beginning as early as September.
peoples.special: Jose Rizal, a doctor and writer executed in 1896, is the national hero of the Philippines.

peoples.home: Brazil, and diaspora in the United States, Portugal and Japan
peoples.s: Brazil is the largest country in South America. Its people have roots in Indigenous, Portuguese, African, and later European and Japanese migration.
peoples.fun: Brazil is the largest Portuguese-speaking country in the world by a wide margin.
peoples.special: Brazil has won the men's FIFA World Cup five times, more than any other country.

peoples.s: Mexico is one of the world's most populous Spanish-speaking countries. Its culture blends Indigenous traditions such as the Maya and Aztec with Spanish influence.
peoples.fun: Mexico City is built on top of Tenochtitlan, the Aztec capital founded in 1325.
peoples.special: The Day of the Dead tradition is on UNESCO's list of the intangible cultural heritage of humanity.

peoples.s: Kazakhs were traditionally nomadic herders on the Eurasian steppe. Kazakhstan, their homeland, is the largest landlocked country in the world.
peoples.fun: Kazakh hunters have trained golden eagles to hunt foxes and hares for centuries.
peoples.special: The yurt, a portable felt tent, was the traditional home of steppe nomads.

peoples.s: Uzbeks are the largest Turkic people in Central Asia. Their cities, such as Samarkand and Bukhara, were great centres of the Silk Road.
peoples.fun: Plov, a rice dish with meat and carrots, is the national dish and is cooked in huge cauldrons for celebrations.
peoples.special: Samarkand, famous for the tiled Registan square, was a capital of the conqueror Timur in the 1300s.

peoples.s: Thailand is the only country in Southeast Asia that was never colonised by a European power. Thai culture blends Buddhist traditions, royal customs and a famous cuisine.
peoples.fun: The Thai name for Bangkok is one of the longest place names in the world.
peoples.special: The traditional Thai greeting, the wai, is a small bow with the palms pressed together.

peoples.s: The Bamar are the largest ethnic group of Myanmar, which is home to more than a hundred ethnic groups. Their Buddhist culture shows in the country's thousands of pagodas.
peoples.fun: Many Burmese people wear thanaka, a pale paste made from tree bark, on their faces as sun protection.
peoples.special: The ancient city of Bagan has more than 2,000 surviving temples and pagodas.

peoples.s: Portuguese sailors led the Age of Discovery in the 1400s and 1500s. Portuguese is now spoken on four continents.
peoples.fun: Portugal's borders have barely changed since 1297, among the oldest in Europe.
peoples.special: Fado, a music of longing and loss, is on UNESCO's list of intangible cultural heritage.

peoples.s: The Dutch built a trading empire in the 1600s and learned to live below sea level by building dikes and polders.
peoples.fun: There are more bicycles than people in the Netherlands.
peoples.special: About a quarter of the Netherlands lies below sea level.

peoples.s: Swedes are known for design, innovation and a long tradition of staying neutral in wars. The Vikings from this region once sailed as far as the Black Sea.
peoples.fun: Fika is a Swedish daily coffee break with something sweet, and it is taken seriously.
peoples.special: The Nobel Prizes were created by the Swedish inventor Alfred Nobel's will in 1895.

peoples.s: Norway is a land of fjords and long winters. Norwegians produced great explorers, and their Viking ancestors reached Iceland and Greenland.
peoples.fun: Friluftsliv, or open-air living, is a way of life in Norway, and many people ski before they can read.
peoples.special: Roald Amundsen, a Norwegian, led the first expedition to reach the South Pole in 1911.

peoples.s: Denmark is one of the oldest kingdoms in the world. Danes are known for design, windmills and a strong sense of trust in each other.
peoples.fun: Lego bricks were invented in Denmark, and the name comes from the Danish words leg godt, meaning play well.
peoples.special: Hygge, a feeling of cosy togetherness, is a Danish idea that spread around the world.

peoples.s: Finns speak a language unrelated to most of their neighbours. Finland is known for forests, lakes and a school system admired around the world.
peoples.fun: Finland has about three million saunas for roughly five and a half million people.
peoples.special: Linus Torvalds, a Finn, created the Linux operating system in 1991.

peoples.s: The Czechs lived in the Kingdom of Bohemia for centuries. In 1989 the Velvet Revolution ended communist rule peacefully.
peoples.fun: Czechs drink more beer per person than any other nation.
peoples.special: The word robot comes from Czech writer Karel Capek's 1920 play R.U.R.

peoples.home: Hungary, Romania, Slovakia, Serbia, and diaspora
peoples.s: Hungarians, or Magyars, arrived in Central Europe in the late 800s. Their language is unrelated to nearly all of their neighbours.
peoples.fun: Hungarians write the family name first and the given name second.
peoples.special: Erno Rubik, a Hungarian architecture professor, invented the Rubik's Cube in 1974.

peoples.s: Romanian is a Romance language that grew from the Latin spoken by Roman settlers, surrounded by Slavic neighbours. Romanians live in the lands of the Carpathian Mountains.
peoples.fun: Romania's Parliament Palace is one of the heaviest buildings in the world.
peoples.special: Nadia Comaneci scored the first perfect 10 in Olympic gymnastics in 1976.

peoples.home: Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, Croatia
peoples.s: Serbs are a South Slavic people with a medieval kingdom, Orthodox Christian traditions and a language written in both Cyrillic and Latin letters.
peoples.fun: Serbian is one of the few languages that officially uses two alphabets.
peoples.special: Nikola Tesla, born to a Serb family, pioneered alternating current electricity.

peoples.s: The Bulgars founded one of Europe's oldest states in 681. The Cyrillic alphabet was developed in Bulgaria and spread across the Slavic world.
peoples.fun: In Bulgaria, shaking the head means yes and nodding means no.
peoples.special: Bulgaria is the birthplace of the Cyrillic script, created by disciples of Cyril and Methodius around 900.

peoples.pl: about 67 million in the United Kingdom
peoples.s: The British include English, Scottish, Welsh and Northern Irish people. Britain started the Industrial Revolution and once ruled the largest empire in history.
peoples.fun: British English has hundreds of regional accents, and the tea habit is part of daily life.
peoples.special: The Magna Carta of 1215 limited the power of the king and influenced later democratic ideas.

peoples.lang: English, Spanish, and hundreds of other languages
peoples.s: Americans descend from Indigenous peoples and from immigrants from nearly every country in the world. The United States became independent in 1776.
peoples.fun: The United States has no official language at the national level.
peoples.special: More than 350 languages are spoken at home across the United States.

peoples.lang: English, French, and many Indigenous languages
peoples.s: Canada has two official languages and one of the most diverse populations in the world. Most Canadians live within a few hours of the southern border.
peoples.fun: Canada has the longest coastline of any country in the world.
peoples.special: The maple leaf has been a symbol of Canada for centuries, and it appears on the national flag.

peoples.s: Most Australians live in cities along the coast. The country is home to the oldest living cultures on Earth, plus waves of migrants from across the world.
peoples.fun: Australia has more kangaroos than people.
peoples.special: Australia is both a country and a continent.

peoples.s: Egyptians live mostly along the Nile, as people have for over 5,000 years. Ancient Egypt built the pyramids and a writing system of hieroglyphs.
peoples.fun: About nine in ten Egyptians live on just a few percent of the land along the Nile.
peoples.special: The Great Pyramid of Giza was the tallest human-made structure in the world for nearly 4,000 years.

peoples.s: Argentina's people mostly descend from Spanish and Italian immigrants. The country is known for tango, football and vast grasslands called the pampas.
peoples.fun: Tango began in the port neighbourhoods of Buenos Aires and Montevideo and is on UNESCO's heritage list.
peoples.special: Argentina has won the FIFA World Cup three times.

peoples.s: Colombians come from Indigenous, Spanish and African roots. The country is known for coffee, emeralds and a rich variety of music.
peoples.fun: Colombia is one of the world's top coffee producers.
peoples.special: Gabriel Garcia Marquez's novel One Hundred Years of Solitude, from 1967, made Colombian writing famous worldwide.

peoples.s: Peru was the heart of the Inca Empire. Peruvians live in coastal desert, high Andes and Amazon rainforest.
peoples.fun: Peru is home to thousands of native potato varieties.
peoples.special: Machu Picchu, the Inca citadel high in the Andes, was built in the 1400s.

peoples.s: Chile is a long, narrow country stretching more than 4,000 kilometres along the Pacific coast. Chileans are known for poets and wine.
peoples.fun: Chile is so long that it spans deserts, glaciers and rainforest.
peoples.special: Two Chileans have won the Nobel Prize in Literature, Gabriela Mistral in 1945 and Pablo Neruda in 1971.

peoples.s: Cuba's people have Spanish, African and Indigenous roots. The island is known for music, cigars and its vintage cars.
peoples.fun: Many cars on Cuban roads are American models from the 1950s.
peoples.special: Cuban son, a blend of Spanish guitar and African rhythm, helped inspire salsa.

peoples.s: Venezuela has Indigenous, Spanish and African roots. Simon Bolivar, who led independence across northern South America, was born in Caracas.
peoples.fun: Angel Falls in Venezuela is the world's tallest uninterrupted waterfall, at 979 metres.
peoples.special: Venezuela has some of the world's largest known oil reserves.

peoples.s: The Kyrgyz are a mountain people whose herders still move livestock to high summer pastures. The Manas epic, sung by storytellers, is one of the longest oral poems in the world.
peoples.fun: The Kyrgyz play kok-boru, a horseback game in which two teams carry a goat carcass to a goal.
peoples.special: Traditional felt carpets called shyrdak are made by hand and decorated with symbols of nature.

peoples.s: Tajiks are a Persian-speaking people of Central Asia, living among high mountains. Their culture is closely tied to the poetry and learning of the old Persian world.
peoples.fun: Tajikistan is more than 90 percent mountains, and the Pamirs are called the Roof of the World.
peoples.special: Rudaki, who lived in the 800s and 900s, is often called the father of Persian poetry.

peoples.pl: about 30 million, in Azerbaijan and Iran
peoples.s: Azerbaijanis speak a Turkic language and live in the Caucasus and northwest Iran. Baku, their capital on the Caspian Sea, grew rich from oil more than a century ago.
peoples.fun: Azerbaijan is often called the Land of Fire because natural gas flames have burned there for ages.
peoples.special: Uzeyir Hajibeyov wrote Leyli and Majnun in 1908, the first opera in the Muslim world.

peoples.s: Georgians speak a language unrelated to any of their neighbours and write it in their own alphabet. Their kingdom flourished in the Middle Ages.
peoples.fun: Georgians make wine in clay vessels called qvevri, a method about 8,000 years old.
peoples.special: Georgian is written in a unique alphabet that UNESCO lists as intangible cultural heritage.

peoples.pl: about 4 million in Croatia, with many more abroad
peoples.home: Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and diaspora
peoples.s: Croats live along the Adriatic coast and in the lands inland. Croatia became independent in 1991 and joined the European Union in 2013.
peoples.fun: The necktie is said to take its name from Croatian soldiers who wore scarves in the 1600s.
peoples.special: The old city walls of Dubrovnik are one of the best preserved in Europe.

peoples.s: Lithuania was once one of Europe's largest states. Lithuanian is among the oldest living Indo-European languages.
peoples.fun: Lithuanians are among the world's top basketball fans, and the sport is treated almost like a national religion.
peoples.special: In 1990 Lithuania became the first Soviet republic to declare independence.

peoples.s: Estonians speak a language related to Finnish, not to their Baltic neighbours. Estonia is one of the most digital countries in the world.
peoples.fun: Skype was created by Estonian developers in 2003.
peoples.special: Estonia's Song Festival, held every five years, draws tens of thousands of singers.

peoples.home: Albania, Kosovo, North Macedonia, and diaspora
peoples.s: Albanians speak a language that forms its own branch of the Indo-European family. They live in Albania, Kosovo and nearby lands, and many live abroad.
peoples.fun: Albanians shake their heads in a way that can look like no to visitors but often means yes.
peoples.special: Mother Teresa, born in Skopje to an Albanian family, won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1979.

peoples.s: Icelanders descend mostly from Norse settlers who arrived in the 800s. Their old sagas are among the great works of medieval literature.
peoples.fun: Most Icelanders have no family name and use their father's first name plus son or dottir.
peoples.special: Iceland's parliament, the Althing, was founded in 930 and is among the oldest in the world.

peoples.home: Somalia, Ethiopia, Kenya, Djibouti, and diaspora
peoples.s: Somalis share one language, one main religion and a tradition of poetry. Many were herders of camels, and today many live abroad.
peoples.fun: Somalia has been called a nation of poets, and poems have been used to settle disputes.
peoples.special: Somali was given an official written form in the Latin alphabet in 1972.

peoples.s: The Xhosa are one of South Africa's largest peoples. Their language is known for its three kinds of click sounds.
peoples.fun: Xhosa uses click consonants that are written with the letters c, q and x.
peoples.special: Nelson Mandela was born into the Xhosa people, and his clan name, Madiba, is used with affection across South Africa.

peoples.s: The Akan are the largest people of Ghana. The Ashanti Empire grew rich on gold and trade before the colonial period.
peoples.fun: Adinkra symbols, printed on cloth, each stand for a proverb or idea.
peoples.special: The Golden Stool is the sacred symbol of the Ashanti nation.

peoples.s: Native Hawaiians descend from Polynesian voyagers who crossed the Pacific more than a thousand years ago. Their language and culture are being revived.
peoples.fun: The Hawaiian alphabet has only 13 letters: five vowels and eight consonants.
peoples.special: Polynesian navigators crossed thousands of kilometres of open ocean using stars, waves and birds, with no instruments.

peoples.s: Tibetans live on the highest plateau in the world, and their culture is shaped by Tibetan Buddhism. The Dalai Lama has been their spiritual leader for centuries.
peoples.fun: Tibetans drink butter tea, made with tea, yak butter and salt, many times a day.
peoples.special: The Tibetan Plateau averages over 4,500 metres above sea level.

peoples.s: Malays have lived along the coasts and rivers of the Malay world for centuries. Malay has been a trading language across Southeast Asia.
peoples.fun: Malay is the ancestor of Indonesian, so speakers of both can often understand each other.
peoples.special: The Melaka Sultanate was a great trading port in the 1400s.
